policy: Every requirement below is bound to a verbatim excerpt from the Danish Immigration Service page named in source_roles. Nothing is paraphrased into an excerpt and nothing is inferred. No excerpt text was typed: each is resolved from LINE NUMBERS out of a numbered dump by scripts/visa-registry/excerpts-from-lines.mjs, which fails the file unless both the display and lowercase forms occur literally in the normalized text.
structure_note:
THIS ROUTE HAS TWO TIERS AND THE SECOND ONE IS NOT OPTIONAL. Denmark publishes basic requirements AND four supplementary requirements, and at least TWO of the four must be met — meeting the basic requirements alone does not qualify anyone. Meeting all four instead reduces the residence requirement from eight years to four. So the supplementary tier is simultaneously a floor and an accelerator, and publishing the basic list on its own would tell a reader they qualify when they do not.

The four supplementary requirements are: Danish language test 3, four years' employment in the last four years and six months, the active citizen exam or documented active citizenship, and an average annual taxable income of DKK 346,155.57 at 2026 level.

THE EMPLOYMENT REQUIREMENT IS A RATIO, NOT A DURATION. Three years and six months of regular full-time work WITHIN THE PAST FOUR YEARS. Quoting the 3.5-year figure without its four-year window would let someone count work from a decade ago.

AND 'FULL-TIME' HAS A NUMBER. Thirty hours a week, or 120 a month, combinable across jobs — and the authority publishes an explicit list of what does NOT count, including wage-subsidised positions, unpaid work, job rotation, and any period below the 30-hour line.
freshness_note: No dateline. The income threshold carries its own year in the text ('DKK 346,155.57 (2026 level)') and the page's worked example runs to 2028, so a revision surfaces as a text change to the daily sync.
not_extracted: The full sentencing table — roughly twenty categories of sentence each with its own exclusion period, at lines 100 to 132. The general rules ARE extracted; the table is a schedule of criminal-law consequences that would need a lawyer's reading of any individual case, and publishing it as a checklist would invite exactly that misuse.
The full list of qualifying and disqualifying social benefits, which the authority publishes on a separate linked page.
The registration procedure and dates for the active citizen exam.
The step-by-step application walkthrough and document checklists.

The separate permanent-residence routes the catalogue enumerates alongside this one — for 18-to-19-year-olds, on strong attachment to Denmark, for retired employees of international organisations, and for Greenland and the Faroe Islands.
